learningOutcomes.description: Recognise, describe and extend patterns in numbers and other mathematical situations.
Use number sequences and visual or geometric patterns to make observations, predictions and explanations.
Identify and explain patterns involving whole numbers, including relationships among numbers.
Identify and describe points, line segments, lines and rays using appropriate mathematical language and notation.
Recognise, classify and compare angles and understand relationships between lines and angles.
Use geometric reasoning to analyse figures involving lines, line segments, rays and angles.
Explore numbers through puzzles, arrangements and everyday situations and explain the patterns observed.
Use properties of numbers and operations to solve number-based problems and justify conclusions.
Investigate special number arrangements and develop systematic strategies for solving number puzzles.
Collect, organise and represent data using appropriate tables and graphical representations.
Read and interpret data presented in tables, pictographs, bar graphs and other representations.
Use data to compare quantities, identify patterns and make reasonable inferences.
Identify and use factors and multiples of whole numbers in mathematical situations.
Recognise prime and composite numbers and use divisibility ideas to analyse numbers.
Find and apply common factors, common multiples, prime factorisation and related number relationships.
Understand perimeter as the distance around a closed figure and calculate the perimeter of common shapes.
Understand area as the measure of a surface and determine areas using appropriate units and methods.
Apply perimeter and area concepts to solve problems involving rectangles, squares and other plane figures.
Represent fractions as equal shares and locate and compare fractions using visual and numerical representations.
Recognise equivalent fractions and use common denominators or other strategies to compare and order fractions.
Perform addition, subtraction and other appropriate operations with fractions in meaningful contexts.
Use a ruler and compass to construct and investigate geometric figures accurately.
Construct circles and identify the centre, radius and related geometric features.
Follow construction steps, observe geometric properties and verify constructions through measurement and reasoning.
Identify symmetry in familiar objects, figures and patterns and describe repeated arrangements.
Identify lines of symmetry and determine whether figures have mirror symmetry.
Explore rotational patterns and recognise symmetry in geometric and real-world designs.
Understand integers as numbers that include positive numbers, zero and negative numbers, and represent them on a number line.
Compare and order integers using their positions on the number line and interpret positive and negative quantities in context.
Use addition and subtraction of integers to solve problems involving changes, directions and quantities on either side of zero.
Describe science as a way of observing, questioning and explaining the world.
Identify observation, questioning, prediction and investigation as parts of scientific inquiry.
Use simple everyday situations to frame questions and suggest ways to investigate them.
Group plants using seed type, roots, venation and other observable features.
Group animals using movement, body features and habitat.
Explain how adaptations and biodiversity relate to different habitats and human actions.

chapters.title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

learningOutcomes.description: Identify major nutrients and relate them to their functions and food sources.
Use simple tests for starch and fats and interpret observations.
Explain the importance of a balanced diet, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water for health.
Identify magnetic and non-magnetic materials and the two poles of a magnet.
Describe attraction, repulsion and the north-south alignment of a freely suspended magnet.
Use magnets and simple magnetic arrangements to investigate magnetic behaviour.
Measure length using standard units and suitable measuring instruments.
Convert between common units of length and estimate/measures dimensions.
Describe motion relative to a reference point and distinguish linear, circular and oscillatory motion.
Recognise matter and classify materials using observable properties.
Classify materials as transparent, translucent or opaque and as soluble or insoluble in water.
Select materials for objects by considering properties such as hardness, lustre, flexibility and interaction with water.
Distinguish temperature from the sensation of hotness or coldness.
Read laboratory and clinical thermometers and identify their ranges and least counts.
Convert between Celsius and Fahrenheit for values used in the chapter and interpret temperature observations.

chapters.title: A Journey through States of Water

learningOutcomes.description: Describe water in solid, liquid and gaseous states and the changes between them.
Explain evaporation, condensation and cooling in everyday situations.
Relate the water cycle and responsible water use to observations of water in the environment.

chapters.title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

learningOutcomes.description: Explain why mixtures are separated and select suitable separation methods.
Distinguish methods such as handpicking, sieving, filtration, decantation and evaporation.
Relate separation methods to particle size, solubility, density and practical situations.
Identify essential characteristics of living beings and distinguish living from non-living objects.
Describe plant, mosquito and frog life cycles and major stages.
Plan simple investigations involving germination, growth, respiration or response to conditions.
Identify air, water, soil, sunlight, forests and minerals as natural resources.
Distinguish renewable and non-renewable resources and explain responsible use.
Explain how human activities affect forests, soil, air and water and propose conservation actions.
Identify the Sun, Moon, planets, stars, satellites and constellations in the Solar System context.
Recognise patterns such as Orion, the Big Dipper, Little Dipper and the Pole Star.
Explain simple observations of the night sky and the apparent daily motion of celestial objects.
